title: CorticalLoop → Alavirta: make the predictive residual computable
summary: CorticalLoop (June 2026) adds signed-velocity feedback from a geometric-neuron-style arrow to a multiscale grid, maintaining a 1-D position during sensory blackout. Alavirta (July 2026) explicitly calls itself the child that supplies the missing descending renderer: an abstract internal model can now predict a signal in the recognizer's delay-space coordinates, enabling a reliability-weighted sensory residual, phase/rate correction and a simple action arm. These are engineered synthetic demonstrations, not learned cortex or video prediction.

nodes.claim: Closes a geometric-neuron-derived feedforward readout stack into a recurrent one-dimensional position estimator: a signed arrow/velocity advances a grid and a theta-gated comparator corrects against visible input.
nodes.survived: On the published 1-D circular synthetic track, mean error is 0.0085 with feedback versus 0.0619 without; during a 350-step blackout the errors are 0.024 and 0.247. A direction-blind single channel fails backward travel (0.29 versus 0.002); four incommensurate grid modules disambiguate what one module maps to 287 aliases. Companion grid_discovery.py extracts four dominant linear oscillatory scales from multichannel Takens+DMD with supplied calibration speed.
nodes.killed: The original basis frequencies, quadrature sensors, theta window and CA1-like proportional correction are fixed by design. The DMD companion only discovers dominant linear modes in a synthetic sinusoidal scene, needs known calibration velocity and does not learn nonlinear receptive fields. There is no reported held-out real-world navigation, biological grid network or live-video model.

nodes.claim: Adds a descending renderer from internal oscillator latent state to a predicted Takens delay vector so prediction and reality can be compared in the same sensory coordinates, and uses the residual for precision-weighted phase/rate correction.
nodes.survived: In its reported 2600-step synthetic scalar-oscillator suite, settled phase error is 0.013 rad closed versus 1.566 without residual. The 350-step blackout drifts 0.349 rad and re-locks at 0.122; dynamic signal-roughness precision cuts fog error to 0.067 versus 0.248 fixed-high. Adaptive frequency error after a step is 0.0008 versus 0.130 without frequency adaptation. A minimal action arm reduces amplitude surprise to 0.083 versus 0.750 with action disabled.
nodes.killed: One scalar sinusoid with an analytic cosine renderer, engineered state and correction; the renderer form is not learned. Sensory reliability is a roughness proxy, and motor action changes one amplitude parameter. No unfamiliar visual data, learned appearance decoder, realistic biological neuron, calibrated model uncertainty, or end-to-end video world model is established.

edges.why: The CorticalLoop lineage explicitly names the geometric-neuron / skew-island arrow as a source of signed direction. V9 is a documented antecedent to this operator theme, but the README does not prove direct V9 code inheritance.

Alavirta explicitly calls CorticalLoop its parent and adds the missing top-down renderer that expresses internal predictions in recognizer delay-space coordinates. Its simplified oscillator is a stand-in, not an integration of the complete grid circuit.

Alavirta explicitly names GeometricNeuronV21 as the recognizer it hopes to integrate, while its demonstration uses a bare Takens delay embedding. No V21 controller or original ecg.json pulse is reproduced.

motifs.title: An internal prediction only corrects perception in a shared measurement basis
motifs.description: CorticalLoop shows continued internal state motion through absent input. Alavirta adds the map from that state to predicted sensory coordinates so a measured residual can correct phase and rate, with sensor reliability controlling the gain. The existing results rely on specified state, oscillator and observation structure; learning the basis and renderer on unseen multichannel input is unresolved.
